  • Health

  • 101 shares Dementia has made me question whether my life is still worth living

My mum lived with dementia for 8 years. My adult son & I shared the responsibility. Even when nursing home care becomes inevitable your job is not done. You still have to supervise, advocate for them, negotiate with the care home as well as managing their financial affairs, sell the family home, keep accounts for the Office of the Public Guardian. But I never found the information hard to get & I don't think, for me, a support network would have helped. It wouldn't have stopped the heartbreak, or the exhaustion of coping with the demands alongside a full time job. It wouldn't have stopped me walking the beach in the rain so I could cry freely & the tears wouldn't show as I watched her decline. It wouldn't have stopped me having to sell my vintage (because I'm vintage) childhood teddy to help meet the care costs the government won't help with. The information & support is there already. It's the heartbreak & exhaustion that gets you.
